key_insight: Tucker Attention frames multi-headed self-attention as a Tucker tensor decomposition, providing a single, principled low-rank model that generalizes and recovers existing approximate attention schemes (e.g., GQA, MLA). This unifies disparate heuristics into controllable rank- and core-parameter trade-offs between memory, compute and expressivity.
problem_solved: Reduces the memory and computational footprint of multi-headed self-attention while answering what object existing approximations actually approximate — providing a principled, unified view and design space for approximate attention methods.
method: Model the attention weights/transformations as a multi-way tensor across heads and embedding dimensions and apply a Tucker decomposition (core tensor + factor matrices).
Design parameterizations and rank constraints that recover prior approximate methods (GQA, MLA) as special cases and enable new trade-offs between core size and factor ranks.
Provide efficient implementations and complexity analyses to lower memory use and latency while preserving attention expressivity.
impact: Gives practitioners a theory-driven template to design memory-efficient attention layers with predictable trade-offs, making it easier to compress or accelerate transformers without ad-hoc engineering. It also improves interpretability by exposing which tensor modes and ranks matter most.

paper_title: Tucker Attention: A generalization of approximate attention mechanisms
paper_authors: Timon Klein, Jonas Kusch, Sebastian Sager, Stefan Schnake, Steffen Schotthöfer
